subject: Immediate: Temporary subprocessor addition for SentryEdge — routing & evidence
messages:
From: Claudia Ruiz <claudia@sentryedge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Temporary processing partner (edge vendor) for Oct 10-20 window - notice

Hi Jordan,

For transparency we wanted to notify Redwood that SentryEdge will be adding an interim subprocessor (EdgeTransit LLC) to help with burst routing for the week of Oct 10-20. This is to handle an expected traffic spike for our international test and is temporary — we will not change data retention policies.

Attached: a short declaration and a network routing map that shows the limited egress paths.

Key facts up front:
- Purpose: burst routing for telemetry and health-check pings only (no logs or PII persisted)
- Jurisdiction: traffic will originate from eu-west-1 and transit briefly via EdgeTransit in us-central1 for <3 minutes per session
- Timeline: Oct 10 00:00 UTC to Oct 20 23:59 UTC

Please advise if Redwood needs additional documentation or a formal DPA addendum. If you want, I can loop in our security lead (security@sentryedge.com).

Thanks,
Claudia Ruiz
Head of Ops | SentryEdge
claudia@sentryedge.com

Attachments: sentryedge-temp-processor-declaration.pdf, transit-map-2025-10-04.png

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Claudia Ruiz <claudia@sentryedge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2025 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary processing partner (edge vendor) for Oct 10-20 window - notice

Claudia,

Thanks for the heads up and the attachments. Quick initial questions so we can triage this with SRE and Legal:

1) Will EdgeTransit ever see unredacted request payloads or user identifiers? If so, which fields?
2) Can you confirm whether any telemetry is persisted beyond ephemeral logs? (You indicated no persistence; need explicit confirmation.)
3) Is EdgeTransit covered by SentryEdge's SOC 2 report or an equivalent attestation? If not, do they have an encryption-in-transit & at-rest policy we can review?
4) Please provide a minimal-dataflow diagram (redact any non-essential internals) showing exactly which tokens/headers may touch EdgeTransit.

Laura — can you own the compliance review (I tagged you because procurement/legal will want the attestation). Ben — please flag any billing/plan implications if we would require a temporary routing override.

Claudia, if easier feel free to send a short memo from your security lead — that speeds our review.

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Claudia Ruiz <claudia@sentryedge.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Oct 2025 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary processing partner (edge vendor) for Oct 10-20 window - notice

Jordan / Ben / Claudia,

I reviewed the declaration and the transit map. To proceed quickly we need the following items no later than EOD Oct 8 so we can sign off before your Oct 10 start: 

Required from SentryEdge / EdgeTransit: 
- Signed subprocessor declaration (we need contractor signature on page 2) — we received yours but we need EdgeTransit sign-off.
- Confirmation that no request bodies containing user identifiers (email, user_id, phone) are routed to EdgeTransit. If a token or tracing id is routed, confirm it is pseudonymous.
- EdgeTransit SOC 2 Type II or equivalent attestation, or a filled-in security questionnaire (we can accept ISO/other if SOC unavailable).
- Short retention statement: confirm any logs are retained <24 hours and are automatically purged.
- A minimal dataflow diagram with column for "data types" (PII, telemetry, metrics) and labels for transient vs persisted.

If any of the above are not available, provide the compensating controls and an explicit rollback plan (we won't allow permanent production routing without approvals).

I attached a brief checklist (subprocessor-checklist.xlsx) — please complete and return. If you want a faster path, send EdgeTransit's security lead to a 30-minute call with our security team tomorrow (Oct 7) between 09:00-12:00 PT.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: subprocessor-checklist.xlsx

From: Claudia Ruiz <claudia@sentryedge.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Oct 2025 15:34:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Temporary processing partner (edge vendor) for Oct 10-20 window - notice

Laura/Jordan,

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. Per your checklist:

- EdgeTransit has signed the declaration (attached).
- They will only handle telemetry and health-check pings; no request bodies or PII will be routed. Tracing ids are pseudonymized session tokens — they cannot be mapped back to an email without SentryEdge internal keys.
- EdgeTransit does not have SOC 2 yet; they completed a third-party security assessment by Checkpoint Partners last month. I attached that report (redacted).
- Retention: logs are stored transiently for up to 6 hours for debugging, then auto-purged. No backups.
- Attached: updated transit map (shows a short US egress for <3 minutes), signed declaration, and Checkpoint assessment summary.

We can set up the 30-minute call with EdgeTransit's security lead Wed Oct 8 at 10:30 PT if that slot works for your team. Let me know and we will send calendar invite + dial-in.

Claudia Ruiz
Head of Ops | SentryEdge
claudia@sentryedge.com

Attachments: sentryedge-temp-processor-declaration-edge-signed.pdf, checkpoint-assessment-summary.pdf, transit-map-2025-10-06.png
